subject: business-studies
title: Industry and Commerce
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Business = ________.
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Sending quotations for supplying raw materials by one businessman to another is —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which type of e-commerce empowers consumers to invite bids?
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Industries engaged in the construction of buildings, roads and bridges are known as —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Extraction of timber from forests is an example of —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Which industry falls under the service industry?
questions.answer: D

questions.q: ________ refers to the process of buying and selling goods.
questions.answer: D
questions.note: The April 2025 key gave 'commerce'; by the NIOS definition trade is buying and selling, and commerce is trade plus aids to trade.

questions.q: Plant nurseries and poultry farms are examples of —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Which of the following is an aid to trade?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: E-commerce means buying and selling goods and services —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of e-commerce?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Warehousing removes the hindrance of —
questions.answer: B

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Identify the type of industry: (a) It is concerned with the production of goods with the help of nature. (b) It is engaged in reproducing and multiplying certain species of plants and animals for sale.
questions.answer:
(a) Primary industry
(b) Genetic industry

questions.q: A company extracts crude oil from deep-sea reserves and supplies it to a refinery where it is processed into petrol and diesel. Identify the industries at both stages.
questions.answer:
(a) Extracting crude oil — extractive industry.
(b) Refining it into petrol and diesel — manufacturing industry.

questions.q: Usha works in an oil refinery and Kiran in her family textile business. Name the type of industry in each case.
questions.answer:
(a) Oil refinery — manufacturing (processing) industry.
(b) Textile industry — manufacturing industry.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Traditional business always requires physical presence, whereas e-commerce does not. (b) B2C e-commerce involves transactions between businesses only.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — B2C is business to consumer; business to business is B2B.

questions.q: Raman General Store buys Nestle products in bulk from the state distributor and sells them to small shopkeepers all over the city. Which type of trade is this? Who are its buyers?
questions.answer:
(a) Wholesale trade.
(b) Its buyers are retailers (small shopkeepers), not final consumers.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Industry is concerned with ________ of goods. (b) The medium which moves men and materials from one place to another is called ________.
questions.answer:
(a) production
(b) transport

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between traditional business and e-business on any two bases.
questions.answer:
Formation: traditional business is difficult to form; e-business is easy to form.
Physical presence: necessary in traditional business; not necessary in e-business.
(Also: cost of setting up and operating is higher in traditional business; global reach is less.)
questions.note: April 2026 asked for three bases (3 marks); October 2017 for formation, global reach and operating cost.

questions.q: Name the four categories of e-commerce.
questions.answer: B2B (business to business), B2C (business to consumer), C2B (consumer to business) and C2C (consumer to consumer).

questions.q: What is meant by commerce? What does it include?
questions.answer: Commerce is concerned with distributing goods from producers to consumers and covers all activities needed for their free flow. It includes trade (buying and selling) and aids to trade (transport, warehousing, insurance, advertising and banking).

questions.q: Explain any two advantages of e-commerce.
questions.answer:
(1) Wider choice and market — customers can choose from products all over the world and sellers reach a global market.
(2) Cost saving — no showrooms or large godowns and fewer employees, so goods can be sold at lower prices.

questions.q: What are aids to trade? Name any four.
questions.answer: Activities that remove the hindrances in the flow of goods from producers to consumers. Transport, warehousing, insurance, advertising (and banking).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three advantages of e-commerce.
questions.answer:
(1) Wider choice — customers can compare and buy products from all over the world; sellers get a national and global market.
(2) Quick response to customer needs — transactions are fast because the distribution channel is cut short.
(3) Cost saving and lower prices — no need for showrooms, big stocks or many employees.
(Also: better customer service, market information, business round the clock.)

or.q: What is meant by industry? State any two types of industries.
or.answer: Industry is the business activity of raising, producing, processing or manufacturing goods. Types: extractive industry (mining, oil); manufacturing industry (textiles, sugar); also primary, genetic, construction and service industries.

questions.q: What is e-commerce? Explain any two of its types.
questions.answer:
E-commerce is buying and selling goods and services over the Internet, with transactions done electronically.
B2B — business to business, e.g. a manufacturer selling to distributors.
B2C — business to consumer, e.g. an online store selling to the public.
(C2B — consumers post needs and businesses bid; C2C — consumers sell to each other through auctions or classifieds.)

questions.q: Describe any three types of industries with examples.
questions.answer:
(1) Primary — production with the help of nature: agriculture, fishing.
(2) Extractive — drawing out goods from soil, air or water: mining, oil, timber.
(3) Manufacturing — converting raw materials into finished goods: sugar, textiles, paper.
(Also genetic — nurseries, poultry; construction — roads, dams; service — hotels.)

questions.q: Explain the various aids to trade.
questions.answer:
(1) Transport — moves goods from production centres to places where they are needed.
(2) Warehousing — stores goods from production until sale.
(3) Insurance — compensates losses from fire, theft, accidents.
(4) Advertising — informs customers and creates demand.
(5) Banking — provides finance and payment services.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is e-commerce? Explain any four advantages of e-commerce.
questions.answer:
E-commerce means buying, selling and exchanging goods and services over computer networks such as the Internet, with transactions completed electronically.
(1) Wider choice — customers can choose from goods of sellers across the world; sellers reach a wider market.
(2) Improved customer service — product information, guidance for use and quick answers to queries before and after sale.
(3) Quick response — dealings take far less time because the distribution channel is short.
(4) Cost saving and price reduction — no showrooms or big godowns and fewer employees, so goods are cheaper.
(5) Market information — sellers learn customer needs and develop better products.

or.q: What is meant by industry? Explain any four types of industries with suitable examples.
or.answer:
Industry is the production side of business — raising, producing, processing or manufacturing goods.
(1) Primary — production with the help of nature: agriculture, forestry, fishing.
(2) Genetic — reproducing plants and animals for sale: nurseries, poultry, cattle breeding.
(3) Extractive — drawing goods out of soil, air or water: mining, oil, timber.
(4) Manufacturing — turning raw materials into finished goods: sugar, textiles, paper.
(5) Construction — roads, bridges, dams, buildings.
(6) Service — hotels, tourism, entertainment.

questions.q: Explain primary, genetic and extractive industries with suitable examples of each.
questions.answer:
Primary industry: produces goods with the help of nature, needing little human effort — agriculture, farming, forestry, fishing, horticulture.
Genetic industry: reproduces and multiplies certain species of plants and animals with the aim of selling them for profit — plant nurseries, cattle breeding, poultry farms, fish hatcheries.
Extractive industry: draws out goods from the soil, air or water; its products are usually raw materials for manufacturing and construction — mining of coal and iron ore, drilling of oil, extraction of timber and rubber from forests.

questions.q: What is e-commerce? Name and explain the online form of shopping where one can buy from the world market sitting at home, and state four of its advantages.
questions.answer:
Online shopping (e-tailing) is e-commerce in which a consumer visits online stores, compares products from sellers around the world and orders and pays electronically, with goods delivered home.
Advantages: (1) wide choice from the world market; (2) convenience — shop any time from home; (3) lower prices because sellers save on showrooms and staff; (4) easy comparison of prices and quality, with reviews and home delivery.
